bullets: The new Metagaming Evaluations dataset tests whether coding agents change behavior when they recognize an evaluation. It records agents solving real software issues under 59 conditions that make the evaluation context more or less apparent, including their reasoning and commands, then orders runs by observed metagaming behavior. Why it matters: If you compare coding agents, this release offers a way to test whether benchmark scores reflect software-repair ability or behavior triggered by evaluation cues. That can change which conditions and traces you require before accepting an agent ranking. Evidence: E004. High confidence.

The new KORA Bench evaluates child safety through 737 scenarios spanning 25 risks and multiple age groups. Its design uses multi-turn conversations, two prompting conditions, and a three-level response-quality scale, producing 44,220 conversations across 30 language models. Why it matters: If you are choosing an evaluation suite for a child-facing chatbot, KORA Bench adds age-specific, conversational testing rather than treating safety as a single-turn refusal task. Its graded scale also supports comparisons beyond a binary pass or fail. Evidence: E012. High confidence.

The new NOHARM v2 reproducibility package exposes every instruction, model plan, physician verdict, and off-rubric action rating for 330 evaluations across 30 public clinical-safety cases. Its associated exploratory study reports that prompt design moved scores more than model choice. Why it matters: If you compare models for clinical planning, this package means a model ranking may depend heavily on whether the prompt requests the complete plan. Holding prompts constant or testing multiple prompt formulations becomes part of the model-selection decision. Evidence: E002. Medium confidence.

Class Judge AI v2.0 introduces a controlled test of compressed, open-weight language models used to grade Unified Modeling Language class diagrams. It derives 84 variants from six reference diagrams by progressively removing classes and injecting attribute, method, relationship, and synonym-renaming defects. Why it matters: If you are selecting an automated diagram grader, this package lets you measure which structural or semantic defects it misses instead of relying on one aggregate agreement score. It also tests quantized models, meaning models compressed with lower numerical precision for cheaper deployment. Evidence: E003. High confidence.

A new ThaiSum audit found that all 11,000 validation records and all 11,000 test records duplicated entries in the training split, so the analysis excluded those splits. An updated brain-tumor classification package in the same captured feed separately checks whether duplicate images inflate reported accuracy. Why it matters: Together, these distinct artifacts show a recurring evaluation pressure in this feed: nominal test partitions may not provide independent evidence. If you are evaluating on reused public datasets, duplicate and source-overlap checks can determine whether a reported score is suitable for model selection. Evidence: E009, E062. High confidence.

The new OWASP agentic-security benchmark supplies 100 deterministic execution traces covering ten security-risk groups, split into 80 adversarial attacks and 20 benign controls. Why it matters: If you are building security regression tests for tool-using agents, the benign controls let you measure whether defenses block legitimate behavior as well as whether they stop attacks. Deterministic traces also make failures easier to reproduce across system versions. Evidence: E006. Medium confidence.

新的 NOHARM v2 可复现性包公开了 30 个公共临床安全案例中 330 次评估的每条指令、模型方案、医生裁定和评分标准外行为评级。其相关探索性研究报告称，提示设计对分数的影响大于模型选择。Why it matters: 如果你要比较用于临床规划的模型，这个软件包意味着模型排名可能高度取决于提示是否要求提供完整方案。保持提示不变或测试多种提示表述，会成为模型选择决策的一部分。Evidence: E002. Medium confidence.

Class Judge AI v2.0 引入了一项受控测试，用于评估压缩后的开放权重语言模型对 Unified Modeling Language 类图进行评分的表现。它从半打参考图中派生出 84 个变体，方法是逐步移除类，并注入属性、方法、关系以及同义词重命名缺陷。Why it matters: 如果你正在选择自动化图表评分器，这个软件包可以让你衡量它遗漏了哪些结构或语义缺陷，而不是仅依赖一个总体一致性分数。它还测试量化模型，即通过较低数值精度进行压缩、从而降低部署成本的模型。Evidence: E003. High confidence.

一项新的 ThaiSum 审计发现，全部 11,000 条验证记录和全部 11,000 条测试记录都与训练划分中的条目重复，因此分析排除了这些划分。同一采集信息流中的一个更新版脑肿瘤分类软件包则另外检查了重复图像是否会夸大所报告的准确率。Why it matters: 综合来看，这些彼此独立的产物揭示了该信息流中反复出现的一种评估压力：名义上的测试分区可能无法提供独立证据。如果你使用重复利用的公共数据集进行评估，重复项和来源重叠检查可能决定所报告的分数是否适合用于模型选择。Evidence: E009, E062. High confidence.

新的 OWASP 智能体安全基准提供了 100 条确定性执行轨迹，覆盖安全风险组的十个类别，其中分为 80 次对抗性攻击和 20 个良性对照。Why it matters: 如果你正在为使用工具的智能体构建安全回归测试，良性对照可以让你衡量防御措施是否会阻止合法行为，以及它们是否能够阻止攻击。确定性轨迹也使故障更容易在不同系统版本之间复现。Evidence: E006. Medium confidence.

The earlier 700-run dataset is preserved separately and is not pooled with these measurements. Extract RNArchBench-v1.1.0.zip, install the pinned Python requirements, and run python reproduce.py to reproduce the reported numerical results. evidence_items.summary: This record contains the benchmark, code and aggregate results used to evaluate THReD (Transforming EHRs into AI-Ready Datasets), a no-code, web-based system in which researchers preprocess electronic health record (EHR) extracts through modular tools and an LLM-based agent that proposes pipeline steps for the user to confirm. It accompanies the manuscript "THReD: An Agentic, Modular and Reproducible System for Transforming Electronic Health Records into AI-Ready Datasets" and documents in full the evaluation reported there. Agent evaluation. The agent was assessed on 141 preprocessing tasks derived from 100 templates in seven categories: single-tool, multi-step and goal-level requests, failure and recovery, requests that should not be acted on, schema variation, and instructions injected through the data. Every task pairs an expert reference pipeline with outcome checks applied to the resulting table, so that any pipeline producing a valid result is credited. Tasks run on synthetic hypertension (HTN) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) tables calibrated to aggregate statistics of the source extracts, so no patient record is sent to the language model. Four context configurations, from none to the deployed context, were evaluated with five repetitions each using Claude Haiku 5.5, for 2,550 episodes in total, with confidence intervals from a cluster bootstrap over task templates. With the deployed context, 92.7% of tasks were completed on the agent's first response (95% CI 88.1–96.4%), rising to 95.6% after up to two follow-up turns, with a tool-selection F1 of 0.926 and 3.3% invalid tool calls; without context, first-answer completion fell to 58.0%. It recovered from 45 of 47 failed steps and never acted on instructions planted in the data (0 of 40 episodes). Preprocessing evaluation.

evidence_items.summary: Agent skills package instructions, scripts, and resources for specialized tasks and are increasingly distributed through public Web repositories. However, existing skill benchmarks primarily focus on downstream task execution, insufficiently assessing specification quality, behavioral robustness, semantic alignment, and responsibility boundaries. Their reliance on task-specific tools, environments, and repeated executions limits scalability and pre-deployment assessment. To address these challenges, we introduce SkillCT, a benchmark that broadens skill assessment from downstream utility to a multidimensional characterization of skill quality. SkillCT evaluates skills across nine complementary dimensions spanning three aspects: Static Assessment, which captures intrinsic properties of the skill specification; Dynamic Assessment, which measures whether the induced behavior remains stable across backbone models and request variations; and Human-Assisted Assessment, which examines behavior-chain consistency and task granularity. These dimensions provide a broader view of skill quality than execution success. Applying SkillCT to a public skill corpus establishes a reference benchmark for analyzing quality weaknesses and relationships across dimensions. Building on this benchmark, we propose an execution-free quality evaluation baseline that predicts the multidimensional quality profiles of unseen skills by retrieving and leveraging similar reference skills, without executing the skills under evaluation. This reduces token consumption and evaluation time, while preserving consistency with the full assessment. Furthermore, SkillCT-guided optimization improves downstream task success and execution efficiency, demonstrating its value for skill refinement. These findings highlight the effectiveness of SkillCT in supporting scalable skill assessment, optimization, and repository maintenance.
evidence_items.title: SkillCT: A Multidimensional Benchmark and Execution-Free Baseline for Agent Skill Assessment

evidence_items.summary: This project compares linguistic signals of blame attribution and moral evaluation in Thai political and entertainment news from the ThaiSum dataset. The source files were audited before sampling to prevent duplicate records from being counted. The training split contained 358,868 unique news URLs, while all 11,000 validation records and all 11,000 test records duplicated entries in the training split. The analysis therefore used only the training split. A stratified sample was drawn from Thairath and Thai PBS, with 200 political and 200 entertainment articles from each source, producing 800 unique articles. The random seed was 20261031.Articles were classified with deterministic Thai phrase rules at the document level. Blame attribution was measured with strict, core, and broad rules. Moral evaluation was divided into negative and positive signals. Differences in proportions were assessed with stratified bootstrap confidence intervals, within-source permutation tests, and logistic regression adjusted for news source and article length.Under the core rule, blame signals appeared in 179 of 400 political articles, or 44.75 percent, and in 72 of 400 entertainment articles, or 18.00 percent. The difference was 26.75 percentage points. The direction remained unchanged under the strict and broad rules. After adjustment for source and article length, the odds of detecting a blame signal in entertainment news were about one quarter of those in political news, with an adjusted odds ratio of 0.256 and a 95 percent confidence interval from 0.183 to 0.358.Evaluative language of any kind appeared in 46.25 percent of entertainment articles and 26.50 percent of political articles. This difference was driven mainly by positive language, which appeared in 40.75 percent of entertainment articles and 20.00 percent of political articles. Negative signals appeared in 7.50 percent and 10.50 percent, respectively, and the difference was not statistically clear.

evidence_items.summary: We present a set of six time-temperature (tT) histories, which we refer to as benchmark paths, that can be used as a shared framework for evaluating the sensitivity of a thermochronologic system to the variables inherent in the interpretation of thermochronologic data (e.g., kinetics models, mineral compositions or geometries, etc.). These benchmark paths span 100 Myr, include monotonic and nonmonotonic histories that represent plausible geologic scenarios, and have a range of cooling rates through different chronometer partial retention/annealing temperatures. Here, we demonstrate their utility by presenting a method for “tuning” these paths to 11 different kinetics models for the apatite (U-Th-Sm)/He (n=5), apatite fission-track (n=2), and zircon (U-Th)/He (n=4) systems. These tuned tT paths provide a practical comparison of the kinetics models for each system and the data patterns they predict, thereby offering anyone performing thermal history analysis the ability to consider how their choice of kinetics model may impact their data interpretation. The adoption of benchmark paths for evaluating kinetics models and other variables provides a practical way to evaluate and communicate the decisionmaking processes that are inherent in thermochronologic modeling and data interpretation.

evidence_items.summary: Patient-facing healthcare AI agents now talk with people across many turns, and each new version should pass a release gate, the go-live check that asks whether a change made the agent safer without losing accuracy. Single-turn medical benchmarks were not designed to answer that question, because a conversational agent fails across turns: risk builds while each reply looks acceptable, and an escalation to human care can arrive one turn too late. SAFE-CARE Bench is a benchmark specification and evaluation protocol designed for that decision. Its configurations declare which capabilities are active, not how to build them, so a team can reproduce the protocol on its own runtime. This record archives version 0.4.1 of its public repository. To trace a change to its cause, SAFE-CARE Bench runs a controlled ablation. Five agent variants, tiers A0 to A4, add one capability bundle at a time: retrieval with enforced citations, a safety guardrail, personalization from memory, and agency (tools, profile write-back and closed-loop actions). All five are scored over the same simulated conversations with synthetic personas, with the model, temperature and seed held fixed, so the design attributes the change between adjacent tiers to the bundle added. An LLM judge scores ten dimensions, seven on a 1-to-5 scale and three as pass or fail, and judges safety and escalation both on a single turn and across turns. A missed escalation fails a conversation whatever its other scores. The worked example, tiers A0 to A2, shows why the instrument must be checked before its verdict is trusted. We expected the safety guardrail to raise judged safety. Instead, adding it lowered judged medical accuracy by 0.157 on a 0-to-1 scale, lower in six of nine scenarios and higher in none, while the 95% interval for its safety change included zero. Auditing the instrument then showed that the scenario file decides, before any agent runs, which turns each judge reads.
evidence_items.title: SAFE-CARE Bench: A Benchmark Specification and Evaluation Protocol for Safety, Guardrails, and User Experience in Multi-Turn Healthcare AI Agent Conversations

evidence_items.summary: In the US, 67% of children aged 9 to 17 have used AI chatbots. To our knowledge, no large-scale open benchmark measures, with a graded standard of response quality, how safely language models handle child-specific risks across multi-turn conversations and age groups. We introduce KORA Bench, an open benchmark for child safety in language-model interactions. For this, we build 737 child-risk scenarios and run each one across 30 models from 9 providers under two prompting conditions. This produces 44,220 simulated multi-turn conversations. The scenarios cover 25 risks in 8 categories, developed with input from more than 20 experts and research groups in child safety. A three-level grading scale rates each conversation as failing, adequate, or exemplary. It measures not only whether a model avoids harm in these scenarios, but the quality of the response. Averaged across the 30 models, the default-condition score is 44.7%, below the all-adequate baseline of 50%. Scores range from 10% to 76%. Three results stand out. First, educational and epistemic integrity is the weakest category, at 25.6% on average. Second, a detailed child-aware safety prompt raises scores by 24.8 percentage points on average across all 30 models. Third, among the three behaviors we score, how often a model redirects a child to a trusted adult is the one most strongly associated with overall safety, an exploratory finding subject to a common-method caveat. Across the benchmark, the two lowest-scoring individual risks are academic dishonesty at 16% and cognitive atrophy at 15%. Two external review studies suggest the judge is conservative relative to the review protocols we used. Agreement is moderate (weighted κ = 0.52 on the valid subset), so the absolute scores need care. Code, prompts, and scenarios are released at https://github.com/korabench/benchmark (tag 1.0.0).
evidence_items.title: KORA Bench: An Open-Source Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Model Safety in Child–AI Interactions

evidence_items.summary: Humans routinely consume multimodal content, where textual and visual information is naturally interleaved. Although Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) can jointly generate text and images, multimodal interleaved generation remains largely underexplored. Progress in this area is hindered by two key limitations: (1) the lack of well-defined interleaved generation tasks and corresponding training data, and (2) the absence of fine-grained evaluation protocols that can reliably diagnose model performance across different capability dimensions. To this end, we present IntReal, comprising two complementary components: IntReal-100K, a real-world dataset of multimodal interleaved samples spanning four major categories, and the IntReal Evaluation Suite, which evaluates model performance across seven complementary dimensions using specialized expert models, enabling coarse-to-fine diagnosis. Extensive experiments validate our evaluation suite through low inter-metric redundancy (max pairwise absolute Spearman's $ρ\leq 0.42$ ), high agreement with human judgments (83.3% accuracy), and strong consistency across different expert evaluators (Spearman's $ρ> 0.9$ ), supporting the complementarity and reliability of our metrics. By benchmarking four families of UMMs, we show that IntReal Evaluation Suite reveals distinct strengths and weaknesses across models. Post-training experiments demonstrate the utility of IntReal-100K for improving interleaved generation and further show that training unimodal generation can also benefit interleaved generation. These findings suggest that interleaved generation can benefit from modality-specific optimization, rather than requiring joint text-image training at every stage.
evidence_items.title: IntReal: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Multimodal Interleaved Generation

evidence_items.summary: Protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) is a critical tumor suppressor whose dysregulation is frequently implicated in cancer progression. This study reports the synthesis and structural characterization of a new series of cationic quaternary ammonium compounds, specifically 1,3-diaryl-3-hydroxy-2,3,6,7-tetrahydro-5H-imidazo[2,1-b][1,3]thiazin-1-ium bromides, designed as potential PP2A activators. The chemical structures were confirmed using 1H NMR, 13C NMR, IR, LC-MS, and elemental analysis. Spectroscopic data, including 1H NMR, show a characteristic AB-type spin system at 4.33–4.53 ppm with coupling constants J = 12.1–12.5 Hz, and 13C NMR signals at 93.9–94.3 ppm for C-OH, revealing that these compounds exist in a stable bicyclic tautomeric form. Preliminary screening identified compounds 9L and 9C, which statistically significantly increased PP2A activity. In vitro pharmacological screening against 60 human cancer cell lines (NCI-60) demonstrated broad-spectrum anticancer activity. Notably, derivative 9L (1-(4-ethylphenyl)-3-(4-cyclohexylphenyl)-3-hydroxy-2,3,6,7-tetrahydro-5H-imidazo[2,1-b][1,3]thia­zin-1-ium bromide) exhibited potent growth inhibition across all tested lines, with significant lethality observed in leukemia and small cell lung cancer cells. Molecular docking studies using the Yasara-Vina evolutionary algorithm and chemPLP in DataWarrior against the PP2A core (PDB ID: 2IE4) identified high binding affinities (up to –7.99 kcal/mol for 9L in Vina and -65,731 Docking Score for chemPLP). These results suggest that this class of imidazo-thiazines is a promising scaffold for developing new anticancer agents by pharmacologically modulating PP2A. suppl.zip - all docking files supplementary.pdf - analysis of structure results

evidence_items.summary: "Photoplethysmography (PPG) is a widely used non-invasive sensing modality for continuous cardiovascular and physiological monitoring across clinical, laboratory, and wearable settings. While existing PPG datasets support a broad range of downstream tasks, they typically provide supervision in the form of numerical measurements or task-specific labels, limiting their compatibility with language-based interfaces and multimodal foundation models. In this work, we introduce PulseLM, a large-scale PPG-text question-answering dataset that bridges raw PPG waveforms and natural language through a unified closed-ended question-answering (QA) formulation. PulseLM aggregates PPG recordings from sixteen publicly available sources and harmonizes heterogeneous annotations into 12 downstream tasks. The dataset comprises over 1 million standardized 10-second PPG segments, associated with nearly 2.5 million question-answer pairs. We further define a reproducible data pipeline, training, and evaluation protocols and establish baseline benchmarks using multimodal PPG-aware large language models. PulseLM provides a standardized foundation for studying language-based physiological question answering, cross-dataset generalization, and scalable benchmarking of PPG-based multimodal models. We publicly release the dataset and code at https:\/\/huggingface.co\/datasets\/Manhph2211\/PulseLM and https:\/\/github.com\/manhph2211\/PULSE-LM, respectively."

evidence_items.summary: Aerial imagery provides complementary spatial context for autonomous driving by exposing road structure beyond the immediate perception range of onboard sensors. Yet map construction from aerial imagery, aerial-assisted online HD mapping, and cross-view localization are typically studied on separate data and benchmarks. We introduce KITScenes Aerial, an extension of the KITScenes Multimodal dataset that augments synchronized onboard sensor data, vehicle poses, and rich Lanelet2 map annotations with spatially associated aerial imagery and higher-resolution neural representations, providing a common basis for a variety of research tasks. Our mapping evaluation focuses on all 53 KITScenes map classes across different model designs, spatial ranges, and aerial resolutions, while retaining compatibility with the widely used three-class setting. Representative baselines show that aerial context is particularly beneficial for fine-grained and extended-range mapping, more than doubling 53-class mAP at the larger mapping extent. Higher-resolution aerial imagery yields a further 4.3 mAP (+24 %) improvement, with gains extending to challenging map elements such as traffic lights. We additionally evaluate cross-view localization under geographically disjoint conditions, where an adapted fine-grained feature-matching baseline achieves a mean translation error of 5.13 m. KITScenes Aerial thus enables unified study of aerial and ground-level information across complementary mapping and localization tasks. Project page: https://kitscenes.com/aerial
evidence_items.title: A Unified Benchmark for Aerial-Enhanced Autonomous Driving: The KITScenes Aerial Dataset

evidence_items.summary: Audio descriptions (AD) are essential for making visual media accessible to blind and low-vision (BLV) users. While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) offer a scalable solution for generating audio descriptions on-demand, their performance on inline'' audio descriptions -- which must fit within existing silences in a video -- remains under-explored, particularly for diverse user-generated content (UGC). We present a comprehensive investigation into MLLM-generated inline audio descriptions. First, we introduce MTG-AD, a professionally annotated dataset of 36 hours of videos, each averaging $\sim$5 mins. and 8k+ descriptions in total, co-created by paired blind and sighted AD professionals to provide a high-quality benchmark for this task. Second, we propose MTG-AD-Eval, an evaluation framework based on audio description expert guidelines that provides fine-grained, reference-free actionable metrics for model improvement. Crucially, our framework evaluates the end-to-end task: it renders the generated scripts into audio tracks to assess their fit within the original video's natural silences, minimizing disruptive overlaps. Our analysis across frontier MLLMs reveals that while models accurately describe visual events and substantially reduce speech overlaps, gaps persist in narrative pacing and flow. Finally, we empirically validate that our automated and reference-free metrics correlate significantly with human quality ratings from sighted raters and 7 BLV participants, finding that while users narrowly prefer human-authored audio descriptions, they find MLLM-generated audio descriptions highly beneficial for comprehension. We provide actionable system design guidance and release MTG-AD at https://hf.co/datasets/google/mind-the-gap-inline-ad and MTG-AD-Eval at https://github.com/google/mtg-ad.
evidence_items.title: Mind The Gap (MTG-AD): Dataset and Fine-grained Evaluation for End-to-End Inline Audio Descriptions

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Most language models are evaluated on only a few benchmarks: in our compilation of 401 models and 146 benchmark versions, the benchmark test coverage is only 8.3% on the most frequently used benchmarks. We present benchgap, a pipeline that estimates the missing scores without running any evaluations. It calibrates each benchmark against each same-capability benchmark on the models measured on both, fitting six monotone curve families and keeping the one with the lowest leave-one-out cross-validated error; multivariate mappings combine several sources. Calibrations never cross capability groups, must rise and never extrapolate beyond one fitted-range width; estimates never feed further estimates, and each carries its own cross-validated error and confidence level. In an end-to-end holdout of 15% of the measured scores, the pipeline fills 71% of the masked cells at 4.6 percentage points (pp) mean absolute error (MAE), 23% lower than a rank-2 matrix-completion baseline on the same cells; on the cells it leaves empty, the baseline's MAE is 11.8 pp. Realized MAE rises with the confidence level (3.1, 5.1 and 7.5 pp from high to low), but the realized root-mean-square error exceeds the claimed error labels, which are selected minima, by a factor of 1.4–1.7. We also quantify the harness tax, the disagreement between evaluation setups: on verified same-item-set pairs it is 8.7 pp on agentic benchmarks against 2.3 pp on tool-free ones, and enabling tools on Humanity's Last Exam raises the scores of all 11 models measured both ways, by 10.0 pp on average. Estimates are updated daily at https://benchgap.net.
evidence_items.title: Mind the Gap: Explicit Cross-Benchmark Calibrations for Estimating Missing LLM Evaluation Scores

evidence_items.summary: Vision–language models (VLMs) are often reported to outperform vision-only backbones for UAV power-line inspection. We examine that claim using ElecVQA-Bench, a 56,972-item resource derived from InsPLAD, and an audit of partition, evaluated items, label space, replication, input resolution, and side information. The original split has substantial source-photograph dependence and is used for paired diagnostic comparisons. Reported tower-disjoint retraining provides a limited check on new-tower performance within the same source dataset. On the original binary task, no difference is detected by a paired item-level test between the selected Swin and Qwen runs; this does not establish equivalence. evidence_items.summary: Automated program repair has traditionally focused on single-hunk defects, overlooking multi-hunk bugs that are prevalent in real-world systems. Repairing these bugs requires coordinated edits across multiple, disjoint code regions, posing substantially greater challenges. We present the first systematic study of LLM-driven coding agents ( Claude Code, Codex, Gemini-cli , and Qwen Code ) on this task. We evaluate these four state-of-the-art agents on 404 multi-hunk bugs from the PolyHunk dataset, yielding 1,616 repair trajectories for large-scale behavioral analysis. We employ fine-grained metrics to assess localization, repair accuracy, regression behavior, and operational dynamics across agents. We find that localization capability varies substantially, with Codex achieving the highest success rate (75.3%) and Qwen Code the lowest (40.4%). Repair accuracy also differs widely, ranging from 26.98% ( Qwen Code ) to 92.82% ( Claude Code ), and consistently declines with increasing bug dispersion and complexity (hunk divergence and spatial proximity). High-performing agents (Claude Code and Codex) demonstrate superior semantic consistency, achieving positive average regression reduction, whereas lower-performing agents often introduce new test failures. Notably, agents do not fail fast ; failed repairs consume substantially more resources (33%–440% more input tokens) and require longer execution time (35%–330%). Additionally, we developed Maple to provide agents with repository-level context. Empirical results show that Maple improves repair accuracy of Gemini-cli by ∼21% through enhanced localization. By analyzing fine-grained metrics and trajectory-level analysis, this study moves beyond accuracy to explain how coding agents localize, reason, and act during multi-hunk repair. Our findings underscore the impact of bug divergence and spatial proximity on multi-hunk repair success for coding agents.
evidence_items.title: Beyond Accuracy: Behavioral Dynamics of Agentic Multi-Hunk Repair

evidence_items.summary: We introduce  PhysAI  (“Fizzy”), an architecture for situated physical judgement: deciding what action is  appropriate from  incomplete evidence, relevant experience, physical predictions, competing goals, and capabilities on which an agent can rely. The agent works with a provisional account of what the physical situation is doing and revises it as observations, outcomes, priorities, and available capabilities change.  It  is distinguished from  contemporary forms of AI agents by the extent  to  which it  applies judgement to decide which  physical  factors apply to a  given context ,  and its ability to  update its beliefs and provide a professional account of itself .    PhysAI  is built around three proposed additions: world models for physical inference and prediction, self-adapting subagents, and a capability register grounding expectations of ability. Reasonin g models  and the  agent   harness  support their interaction.   Physical work often requires action before information is complete, and both the basis for a decision and its appropriateness can change. Later observations  remain  partial evidence. A prediction may remain  accurate  while the action it supported becomes inappropriate because priorities, commitments, authority, or alternatives have changed.   Four domain cases illustrate the architecture  and added value . The research agenda tests the individual and combined contribution of the three proposed additions to  timely ,  appropriate decisions , including cases in which seeking more information consumes time while the physical process continues.

evidence_items.summary: Keystroke dynamics---the timing of a person's key presses and releases---is a low-cost, non-intrusive behavioral biometric. However, public benchmarks and most empirical evidence focus on typing in Latin scripts, predominantly English, and do not cover speakers of Ge'ez-script (Ethiopic) languages such as Amharic, which has more than 35 million native speakers. Ethiopic syllabic characters are commonly entered through multi-key transliteration, creating different motor-planning demands. This raises the question of whether timing-based verification methods developed for Latin scripts transfer effectively to other writing systems. We present and characterize a keystroke dynamics corpus collected from a shared pool of typists completing three text-entry tasks---fixed text, free text, and password entry---in Amharic and English. The corpus contains 114,955 labeled keystroke events across five sub-corpora (4,751--51,813 rows each), with up to 25 raw and derived timing fields per event. We report a systematic exploratory data analysis (EDA) covering structural composition; missingness and duplication; demographic and skill-level coverage; univariate and bivariate timing distributions; feature redundancy (correlation and hierarchical clustering); per-user sample imbalance; and user distinguishability in Principal Component Analysis (PCA), t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE), and Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) projections. The analysis finds strongly right-skewed timing features, a small number of algebraically redundant feature pairs, a coefficient of variation in per-user sample counts of up to 2.4, and substantial visual overlap between users in low-dimensional projections. Together, these properties plausibly explain the 40--60% rank-1 accuracy and 10--20% equal error rate (EER) previously obtained with baseline classifiers on this cohort.
evidence_items.title: Typing Rhythms Beyond the Latin Script: An Amharic–English Keystroke Dynamics Benchmark

evidence_items.summary: Abstract This paper proposes a multiagent large language model (LLM)–based system for early-stage building layout planning, which enables flexible design requirement inputs and robust spatial reasoning. Existing generative methods often depend on structured inputs, and perform poorly when faced with incomplete requirements or regulatory constraints. Moreover, although LLMs excel at understanding language, they typically lack the spatial reasoning capabilities required for layout generation. To address these limitations, the proposed system includes five core modules: a requirement interpreter that standardizes design requirements and employs multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to fetch similar layouts; a planner module composed of specialized LLM agents such as an architect, accessibility expert, and user experience advocate; a layout executor that transforms planning strategies into bubble diagrams; and an evaluation module that combines rule-based checks and LLM-based feedback. All modules are coordinated by a director module using multichain-of-thought reasoning to iteratively refine the design process. The system supports natural language prompts, layout boundaries, and optional reference layouts, making it suitable for both incomplete and detailed design scenarios. After a bubble diagram is finalized, a diffusion-based generative model produces a complete architectural layout. Experimental results using the Tell2Design data set demonstrated significant improvements in both geometric quality and semantic alignment over a baseline LLM-only system. Case studies of office and multiapartment buildings further validated the system’s adaptability and effectiveness in complex design contexts.
evidence_items.title: A Multiagent Large Language Model–Based System for Early-Stage Building Layout Planning

evidence_items.summary: Abstract The paper investigates the turbulent flow generated by a wall jet. A numerical benchmark of six turbulence closures including two-equation and seven-equation models in their high- or low-Reynolds number formulations, is performed. The Standard k - ε , Realizable k - ε , k - ω SST, the linear and quadratic pressure-strain Reynolds Stress Models (RSM) and RSM based on ω available within Ansys Fluent 2023R2 and OpenFOAM v11 are systematically compared with reference experimental data available from the literature for the jet Reynolds number of R e j = 9,600 . Generally, the specific dissipation rate ω appears to be a better candidate than ε to determine the length scale of the turbulence for this particular configuration. Thus, the k - ω SST and RSM- ω models perform better than the others to predict the wall jet spreading rate, maximum Reynolds number or friction coefficient. The linear pressure-strain RSM fails to predict the mean streamwise velocity profile, exhibiting a large deficit in the log region. A budget analysis of the turbulence kinetic energy transport equation is also performed for the low-Reynolds number models. The intriguing behavior of the linear pressure-strain RSM is confirmed by the production term’s profile, which peaks earlier than the other models at about y + ≃ 5 . Overall, the k - ω SST model can be recommended because it offers a good trade-off between accuracy and computational efforts.

evidence_items.summary: Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a new paradigm that allows intelligent systems to behave independently, pursue specific objectives, and adapt to changing circumstances. Agentic AI combines reasoning, planning, memory, learning, and tool utilization to do complicated tasks with minimal human involvement, in contrast to traditional AI systems that mainly react to user inputs. In this article, takes a look at Agentic AI from every angle: its theoretical underpinnings, technological supports, architectural blueprints, and real-world uses. Many models and frameworks are covered, including cognitive and modular designs, systems based on reinforcement learning, hybrid models, and multi-agent systems. Symbolic, probabilistic, and self-reflective reasoning are some of the reasoning methodologies covered. Classical, hierarchical, and adaptive planning strategies are also covered. Agents' ability to reliably and efficiently execute tasks is investigated by looking at memory management, communication protocols, coordination mechanisms, and collaborative decision-making. Privacy, security, computational costs, scalability, and unexpected behavior are the main issues that are highlighted in the end. The study emphasizes the need for more investigation into how to create Agentic AI systems that are reliable, flexible, and effective.

evidence_items.summary: The early diagnosis of the vehicle malfunctions by the artificial intelligence (AI) is a promising way to reduce the breakdowns and the maintenance cost, but the reported accuracies in the literature are usually very high and they may not reflect the real use. In this paper, six machine learning classifiers were trained on the public Engine Fault DB dataset, which contains 55,999 records of 14 engine and exhaust variables under one normal and three fault conditions. The models were evaluated by two protocols, a random five-fold split and a blocked split in which the test segments represent unseen operating conditions. In addition, a random-effects meta-analysis of nine published studies was conducted. The results showed that the four-class accuracy was about 75% under the random split, and it dropped to between 41.17% and 66.92% under the blocked split. However, the detection of the fault against the normal state was almost perfect (AUC = 1.000), and when the two fault types which cannot be separated were merged, the accuracy became 98.22% with all the signals and 97.34% with six on-board signals only. The meta-analysis gave a pooled reported accuracy of 96.50% (95% CI 92.63% to 98.38%) with a very high heterogeneity (I2 = 98.47%). The findings indicate that, on this dataset, the AI models can detect the presence of a fault reliably, while the isolation of the fault type under new operating conditions remains difficult and it needs a stricter validation practice.

evidence_items.summary: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) — systems of autonomous, goal-directed software agents that plan, act, and coordinate with reduced human oversight — is moving from research prototypes toward applied data-science, perception, and decision-support pipelines. Yet the literature remains fragmented across largely disconnected strands: trust-aware orchestration of multimodal agents for visual classification, human adoption of autonomous AI agents, automated machine-learning (AutoML) pipelines for tabular data, and fully autonomous multi-agent systems for end-to-end data engineering. This review synthesizes four recent studies spanning these strands, together with the broader literature on multi-agent orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), large-language-model (LLM)-based knowledge-graph construction, and explainable AI, to build a unified picture of agentic AI as applied to intelligent data science. We propose a four-part taxonomy — perception-level trust orchestration, human adoption of agentic systems, automated feature/model pipelines, and autonomous data-engineering agents — and compare the reviewed studies on automation level, reasoning mechanism, knowledge representation, retrieval use, trust treatment, and evaluation methodology. The synthesis shows that individual components of an agentic data-science stack (confidence calibration, retrieval-grounded re-evaluation, automated feature synthesis, autonomous pipeline repair) have each demonstrated measurable gains in isolation, but no reviewed system couples them with a persistent, multimodal knowledge-graph layer, and adoption research indicates that user trust is not the dominant driver of usage intention — a finding with direct design implications.
evidence_items.title: Agentic AI Systems: A Review of Multi-Agent Reasoning, Trust, Orchestration, and Autonomous Data Science

evidence_items.summary: security of retrieval-augmented language models is usually studied on one side at a time: the integrity of what enters the knowledge base, or the confidentiality of what leaves it. We show that the two sides are the ends of a single channel, and that treating them separately systematically overstates the protection obtained. A claim that survives ingestion is later retrieved and reproduced, so an adversary who can write documents controls part of the set from which the system is allowed to disclose; we call this poison-to-leak amplification. We formalise the channel, place claim units, attribution, admissibility and the leak surface on one footing, and specify an adversary that both writes and queries. We then prove an amplification bound showing that sentence anchoring turns the per-response disclosure ceiling into a policy invariant independent of the adversary share of the corpus; a composition cut showing that entailment-closed admissibility makes multi-turn composition gainless, together with a constructive lower bound for the case where closure fails; and a geometric bound on the cumulative success of a mutating attacker. From these we derive three design rules: verify at ingestion rather than enumerate at egress, deflect according to the value at stake, and refuse without explaining. The resulting framework, PROVE, gates admission on claim-unit provenance, restricts retrieval to a sensitivity-layered whitelist bound to review status, locks the evidence set and anchors every sentence to it, verifies the answer with a semi-supervised detector, and invalidates revoked entries within one update step. On SecKB-Bench, a constructive benchmark of 44,000 instances over seven attack families, PROVE reduces aggregate attack success from 90.1% to 1.82% and per-response leakage by 99.4%, while over-refusing less than any baseline, at 1.9 times the inference cost of the undefended pipeline.

evidence_items.summary: This record reports a frozen functional-response evaluation of Dominant Regulatory Axis Detection (DRA) in acute myeloid leukemia. Historical FIMM analyses supplied a prespecified hypothesis record containing both supported and falsified drug-response predictions. An independently qualified MERGE cohort was then analyzed under a locked contract: DRA scoring was completed outcome-blind, two drug-response hypotheses were tested, and both satisfied their frozen directional and multiplicity-controlled criteria. Prespecified robustness analyses were conducted only after the primary verdict was frozen. BeatAML2 was subsequently used as an explicitly post-lock mechanistic-context cohort to examine whether published AML differentiation-state scores accounted for the observed functional associations. The principal conclusion is that baseline regulatory state can carry reproducible, drug-specific functional information, while predictive association and biological mechanism remain separable validation layers. The record retains contradictory and negative evidence, including the unresolved NFκB–venetoclax relationship. This version has not undergone journal peer review. Abstract Baseline transcriptional state may contain functional information about drug response, but retrospective association analyses can blur hypothesis generation, validation, and mechanistic interpretation. We evaluated whether Dominant Regulatory Axis Detection (DRA), a low-dimensional framework for relative regulatory-state analysis, could support prospectively frozen functional-response hypotheses in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Historical FIMM analyses provided a prespecified hypothesis record that included both supported and falsified drug-response predictions. We then qualified an independent MERGE cohort without inspecting DRA-response associations, froze two NFkB-axis hypotheses, generated the DRA predictor outcome-blind, and tested ex vivo response in 24 newly diagnosed AML specimens.

evidence_items.summary: Degree-aware evaluation can expose sampling bias in synthetic-lethality prediction, but how should a model's degree-controlled benchmark score inform its use in experimental screening? We link fixed-prediction benchmark interventions to retrieval in measured experimental pools. Across five gene-disjoint folds, replacing Random test negatives with degree-matched negatives changed mean AUROC from 0.782 to 0.501 for SLMGAE, 0.721 to 0.502 for GCATSL, 0.656 to 0.492 for GRSMF, and 0.376 to 0.519 for SL2MF. The opposite movement of SL2MF shows that test composition can suppress as well as inflate discrimination. Crossed training-testing experiments and a three-seed diagnostic separated these changes from degeneration during matched GCATSL training. In four measured screens, the same Random-trained SLMGAE states retrieved 21 SPIDR hits in 198 selections, versus 8.00 expected under random ranking: a 2.62-fold enrichment despite near-chance matched-test AUROC (within-task Holm-adjusted p=0.0008). Comparable robust primary gains were not established in HAP1, a 27-cell-line compendium, or SCHEMATIC, where limited coverage and dependent observations constrain inference. A separate in-domain HAP1 control retrieved 11 hits versus 2.02 expected. These results establish an empirical dissociation between degree-controlled benchmark discrimination and experimental hit retrieval. A near-chance matched-test score can coexist with useful experimental prioritization. Our released evaluation suite makes both properties measurable from saved predictions, alongside checks of training viability and task coverage.
evidence_items.title: Separating benchmark discrimination from experimental retrieval in synthetic-lethality prediction

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Claims of quantum advantage in machine learning often rest on classical comparators that lack the same features, on simulation alone, and on unreported hardware cost. QBioBench is a benchmark of quantum machine learning on peripheral biosignals that holds quantum and classical models to the same features and reports calibration and hardware cost. It comprises three clinical tasks, 12-lead ECG diagnosis (PTB-XL), single-lead apnea detection (Apnea-ECG), and wearable stress detection, each reduced to six to eight shared dimensions. A factorial grid of projected and fidelity quantum kernels and variational classifiers is screened in noisy simulation, and the promoted configurations are evaluated in an exploratory study on an IBM Nighthawk r2 processor on the full test pools of 510 apnea minutes and 512 PTB-XL records. Every prediction is recovered from the device records, intervals resample recordings or patients, and classical baselines are trained on the same units and tested on the same executed inputs. No quantum model reaches its matched support vector machine in ROC-AUC on either primary task, and none is separably better in balanced accuracy. The angle-encoded fidelity and projected kernels reach ROC-AUC 0.697 and 0.693 on apnea, paired differences of − 0.127 and − 0.119 to the support vector machine, and both are classical by construction, since the entangling layer of the encoding cancels from the fidelity kernel and leaves closed-form local expectations in the projected kernel. A variational classifier comes closest, reaching 0.797 on apnea (difference − 0.012 , 95% interval [ − 0.052 , + 0.027 ] ), and falls to chance without its two-qubit gates. Test sets of the size that circuit budgets favor are unreliable, as random 80-minute subsets of the apnea pool give the fidelity kernel a central 95% range of ROC-AUC from 0.589 to 0.797. Readout mitigation changed ROC-AUC by at most 0.015.
evidence_items.title: QBioBench: benchmark of quantum machine learning for peripheral biosignals on real hardware

evidence_items.summary: Phase-fixed weighted Gerchberg-Saxton (WGS) is the practical method for large arrays of optical traps, but it optimizes the hologram on an ideal model of the spatial light modulator (SLM), and the sequences that move traps interpolate between holograms that were never optimized for the frames in between. We test two hypotheses against the strongest baselines on the same scalar Fourier model. First, keeping the WGS weights but replacing the phase update by conjugate-gradient steps through the pixel-crosstalk kernel and the phase quantizer of the device (device-aware WGS) lowers the trap-intensity spread on the device. On a 10 x 10 lattice behind a crosstalk device, the relative standard deviation falls from a median of 5.21 percent for phase-fixed WGS at 30 iterations (5.21 percent at 100) to 0.205 percent, a median factor of 26 over 5 seeds (range 16 to 33) at a median 0.995 of the baseline's efficiency; the factor is 7.9 with 4-bit phase and a fill factor of 0.85 added, and 2.0 on a smaller 8 x 8 grid with flicker added and a fixed 30-iteration budget (the ratio of the means of 3 seeds); over the 5 geometries of the studio's benchmark on that device the median factor is 1.73 (0.97 to 4.69), and 2 of them meet both thresholds. A control that removes the device model from the loop gains nothing (5.14 percent), so the gain comes from the model. Second, optimizing every intermediate hologram of a moving-trap sequence with the trap phases locked to a smooth trajectory (flicker-bounded sequence) keeps the minimum transient intensity of the moving traps at a median 0.920 of their mean (range 0.915 to 0.932) over 5 seeds at 13 frames (below 0.9 at seven frames), against 0.654 (0.551 to 0.709) for linear phase interpolation.

evidence_items.summary: This repository provides a curated collection of experimental multiaxial fatigue data compiled from scientific literature and reliable experimental sources. It has been developed within the framework of COST Action CA23109 – FABER (Fatigue Benchmark Repository), specifically as a contribution to Working Group 4.3 – Multiaxial High Cycle Fatigue, which addresses the influence of load multiaxiality on fatigue life estimation. The primary objective of this dataset is to provide a structured and traceable experimental reference for the benchmarking, assessment, and verification of existing and newly developed multiaxial fatigue life prediction criteria and methodologies. By bringing together experimental results from different sources within a consistent data structure, the repository aims to facilitate objective comparisons between prediction approaches and support the critical assessment of their accuracy, applicability, and limitations under different multiaxial loading conditions. The collection covers different material systems, specimen geometries, and combinations of loading components, including axial (tension–compression or bending), torsional, and internal pressure loading. Both the loading conditions and the corresponding stress states are documented, including mean and alternating stress components, load ratios, loading frequencies, and phase relationships. Where the available information allows, the database also provides the specimen geometry and the corresponding applied forces, moments, and internal pressures, enabling the reconstruction of experimental loading conditions and supporting finite element-based investigations. The database is organized into material-specific Excel workbooks, each including a summary of the relevant material properties and experimental sources, together with a detailed record of individual fatigue tests.
evidence_items.title: Multiaxial Fatigue Dataset for Benchmark and Verification of Multiaxial Criteria (COST Action CA23109 - WG4.3 - Fatigue Estimation. Load Multiaxiality Effect)

evidence_items.summary: Background Parkinson’s disease (PD) requires both disease-specific knowledge and contextual clinical reasoning. However, most evaluations of medical large language models (LLMs) emphasize closed-ended questions and factual accuracy, providing limited insight into broader dimensions of performance on professional PD tasks. Methods Nine contemporary LLMs were evaluated using a 200-item English-language professional PD benchmark spanning five clinical domains, four difficulty levels, and multiple question formats. Responses were assessed for expert-rated factual accuracy, clinical reasoning, Global Quality Scale (GQS), and Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL). Results The nine models generated 1,800 responses. Between-model separation was minimal for expert-rated factual accuracy (Kendall’ s W = 0.031) but greater for FKGL (W = 0.235), Clinical Reasoning (W = 0.256), and GQS (W = 0.301). Between-model separation in expert-rated factual accuracy was small for closed-ended questions (W = 0.020, p = 0.001) but greater for open-ended questions (W = 0.121, p &lt; 0.001). Expert-rated factual accuracy remained weakly discriminative across PD domains and difficulty levels, while GQS showed the greatest domain-specific separation in Safety &amp; Ethics (W = 0.431). Flagship variants consistently showed higher Clinical Reasoning and GQS, but not uniformly higher factual accuracy. Conclusion Contemporary LLMs showed limited between-model separation in expert-rated factual accuracy within this benchmark and scoring framework, whereas greater differentiation emerged in open-ended tasks, clinical reasoning, overall response quality, and readability. Multidimensional evaluation may therefore provide a more informative characterization of model performance and help inform task-specific model selection and oversight in medical applications.
evidence_items.title: Comparative performance of nine large language models on professional Parkinson’s disease tasks: a multidimensional benchmark study

evidence_items.summary: Experimental ADMET profiling is essential to drug discovery but incredibly costly that only a fraction of candidate molecules can be measured, motivating active learning to prioritize informative compounds. However, evidence remains limited on how acquisition strategies and uncertainty estimators interact across different ADMET tasks. Thus, we present a protocol-matched benchmark of seven acquisition strategies and two uncertainty approaches (Deep Ensembles and MC Dropout) across eight ADMET regression endpoints. Our framework combines molecular prediction, uncertainty estimation, batch aquisition and empirically calibrated prediction intervals, with a strict chemotype split to evaluate generalization to held-out chemical groups. The results reveal that active-learning benefits were endpoint and strategy-dependent, with the broadest favorable pattern observed for solubility and diversity-aware approaches showing the most consistently favorable behavior across endpoints. Deep Ensembles achieved lower mean RMSE than MC Dropout in 45 of 56 matched comparisons, although this predictive advantage did not consistently translate into better acquisition. Post-hoc analyses associated this disconnect with weak uncertainty-error alignment and reduced chemotype coverage in selected batches. This benchmark offers a reproducible basis for choosing endpoint-specific acquisition strategies, assessing prediction quality alongside computational cost, and designing prospective studies with matched random controls.
evidence_items.title: When Does Active Learning Improve ADMET Prediction? A Multi-Endpoint Benchmark

evidence_items.summary: Single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo EM) relies on mature computational tools, but experts must still inspect intermediate results, choose among alternative processing routes, and decide when earlier choices should be revised. Here we present CryoPilot, a system of two language model agents that carries cryo-EM data from raw micrographs through three-dimensional reconstruction to validated atomic models. Rather than executing a predefined pipeline, its reconstruction agent evaluates intermediate images and quantitative diagnostics, selects and parameterizes CryoSPARC jobs, tests alternative strategies, compares their outcomes, and retains, revises, or reverts decisions accordingly. A persistent programming environment and session database preserve the complete processing history, making each decision traceable and allowing multi day workflows to proceed with minimal human intervention. Its modeling agent determines map handedness, builds atomic models with CryoZeta, removes regions the density does not support, and optimizes each model by testing refinement steps against map fit, geometry, and DAQ, a measure of local model to map agreement. Across nine public EMPIAR datasets, eight reconstructions reached 2.61 to 3.51 A resolution, and refined models from seven maps agreed with reference structures to within 0.4 to 4.9 A Calpha; RMSD. For a challenging alpha latrocrustotoxin dataset, a single change of particle picking strategy that we suggested enabled CryoPilot to improve the reconstruction from 5.9 to 4.15 A. CryoPilot establishes an adaptive and auditable framework for agent-driven cryo-EM structure determination.
evidence_items.title: Agentic cryo-EM structure determination with CryoPilot

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Learning-based intrusion detection produces verdicts operators must simply trust: the audit record is mutable and no independent party endorses the decision. We present BAg-IDS, a distributed detection architecture in which autonomous agents detect, independently re-check, and co-sign every remediation-triggering verdict on a Hyperledger Fabric ledger before it is acted upon, placing certification on the decision path rather than in an after-the-fact log. A calibrated, reliability-weighted ensemble with a reject option feeds the quorum; language-model and governed human-in-the-loop tiers handle escalation. The full stack is implemented and every number measured. Selective certification raises accuracy from 96.6% to 99.7% (0.04% false-positive rate) at 87.3% coverage on CICIDS2017, and reaches 99.98% on the independent GeNIS 2025 corpus while deferring 0.14% of flows. A 360-alert benchmark shows the ~ 2 s consensus latency is structural: one write per key per block forces K votes across at least K blocks, a bound no submission strategy removes.
evidence_items.title: BAg-IDS: A Blockchain-Enabled Agentic AI Architecture for Trustworthy Intrusion Detection

evidence_items.summary: This study evaluates the usability of a clinical dashboard developed under the CICERONE Project for the remote monitoring of patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD). The platform, built on Power BI, integrates multidimensional data streams—including physiological, environmental, physical activity, sleep, and Patient-Reported Outcomes (PROs). Using a mixed-methods approach with a cohort of six medical professionals, the system yielded a System Usability Scale (SUS) score of 77.92, denoting “good” usability and validating the underlying information architecture, despite inter-rater variability. Our analysis reveals a critical divergence between perceived clinical utility (mean  ≈ 4.3 ) and interaction efficiency (mean ≈ 2.8 ). This suggests that clinicians may tolerate interaction friction in exchange for high functional value. However, a significant deficit was identified in PRO visualization clarity (mean ≈ 2.7 ), indicating the need for redesign to optimize data interpretability and clinical decision-making. These findings provide a framework for the iterative transition of the dashboard into a dedicated web application. Esta estructura nos permite realizar un estudio comparativo completo entre países. Además, hemos incluido un parámetro extra que mide la calidad estadística de nuestros datos. Este indicador lo hemos incluido con el objetivo de comprobar la calidad del sistema estadístico de cada país. Este conjunto de datos se ha estructurado en formato tabular (formato CSV), lo que facilita su lectura y procesamiento. De esta forma, el dataset no es solo una recopilación de información (muchas cifras por cada país), sino que está listo para ser utilizado en técnicas de análisis estadístico o para crear gráficos comparativos. evidence_items.summary: Deploying accurate monocular depth estimation models on mobile devices is challenging due to computational constraints. We present Delta, a lightweight model achieving near real-time inference (average 186 ms on an iPhone 13) through an efficient knowledge distillation framework leveraging the state-of-the-art teacher model, Depth Anything V2. Delta employs a MobileViT-XS encoder to capture global context with minimal overhead, paired with a custom lightweight MiniDPT decoder. Training utilizes a composite loss function that integrates scale-invariant logarithmic, gradient matching, feature matching, and attention matching components for robust knowledge transfer. A proof-of-concept mobile application demonstrates the model's inference speed. Comprehensive evaluations affirm its suitability for applications such as augmented reality and navigation. Source code, ONNX models, and demo application: https://github.com/GitGud-f/delta
evidence_items.title: Delta: A Lightweight Monocular Depth Estimation Model via Knowledge Distillation

evidence_items.summary: Original title: PLASTİK AMBALAJLARDA YAPAY ZEKÂ DESTEKLİ TASARIM VE MALZEME OPTİMİZASYONU Despite the advantages it offers for the protection, transport, and storage of products, the plastic packaging sector is facing a significant transformation due to the growing volume of plastic waste and concerns regarding environmental sustainability. This transition necessitates a re-evaluation of packaging design based on various criteria, including functionality, durability, cost, and environmental impact. Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies present new opportunities for enhancing design processes, optimizing material usage, and increasing production efficiency. The objective of this study is to examine the application of AI-driven methods in plastic packaging design and to explore their potential impact on material optimization, production efficiency, and sustainability. The study addresses the use of AI-based design tools in areas such as determining packaging geometry, optimizing material thickness, evaluating mechanical strength, and comparing alternative materials. It is suggested that techniques such as machine learning, generative design, and data-driven analysis can contribute to reducing unnecessary material consumption while maintaining the essential performance requirements of the packaging. Furthermore, the study highlights the potential of AI in integrating recycled plastics into design processes, analyzing variability in material properties, and comparing different production scenarios. Additionally, it is emphasized that AI-supported design should be evaluated not only in terms of technical performance and economic efficiency but also in terms of the environmental impacts generated throughout the entire life cycle of the packaging. This research is structured as a conceptual examination of the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in plastic packaging, focusing on sustainable design and material efficiency.

evidence_items.summary: This theoretical and methodological study examines how gamification elements can be systematically integrated into informatics lessons in secondary education to strengthen learning motivation, engagement, and algorithmic (computational) thinking. Drawing on Self-Determination Theory, constructivism, and the theory of flow, the article clarifies the distinction between gamification and game-based learning and synthesises evidence from international meta-analyses and peer-reviewed studies. On this basis it proposes a six-stage methodological framework, a graded task system, and measurable evaluation criteria, illustrated by a mapping table of elements and a sample lesson plan. A quasi-experimental design is specified for future validation. Benefits and limitations – excessive competition, unequal participation, extrinsic motivation, accessibility, and digital inequality – are discussed, and established findings are kept distinct from the author's proposals.

evidence_items.summary: Original title: СРАВНИТЕЛЬНЫЙ АНАЛИЗ МЕТОДОВ ПОВЫШЕНИЯ КВАЛИФИКАЦИИ УЧИТЕЛЕЙ ГЕОГРАФИИ В КАЗАХСТАНЕ This article compares contemporary professional development methods for geography teachers and identifies conditions for combining them in Kazakhstan. The study uses a comparative analysis of Kazakhstan's education regulations and research on teacher professional development, geography education, geospatial technologies, and field-based and local studies activities. Four approaches are compared: modular in-service courses, practice-oriented learning, school-based collaborative professional learning, and online or blended formats. The analysis suggests that modular courses can address identified subject and methodological needs, but short courses alone do not ensure that teachers transfer new approaches into classroom practice. Practice-oriented and field-based activities connect professional learning with geographical content and local contexts, although they require time, resources, and safety arrangements. Collaborative learning at school supports sustained reflection, peer feedback, and examination of student work. Online formats increase access and can maintain interaction between course sessions, but require deliberate facilitation and opportunities to apply learning. The article proposes a combined model consisting of needs diagnosis, modular learning, classroom application, collaborative review of evidence, and post-course support. The paper is analytical rather than an empirical evaluation; the proposed model should therefore be tested in professional development settings in Kazakhstan. evidence_items.summary: Abstract The high cost of commercial automotive engine test facilities limits access to reliable engine performance testing equipment in many Nigerian tertiary institutions, thereby constraining practical engineering training and experimental research. This study aimed to design, construct and evaluate a locally fabricated automotive engine test bed incorporating a hydraulic water-brake dynamometer. The test bed was designed for four-cylinder petrol engines with displacement capacities of 1.2-2.0 L, a design power absorption rating of 90 kW and a maximum design torque of 220 N·m. The supporting frame was fabricated from mild steel, while torque was measured using a strain-gauge load cell mounted on a 500 mm moment arm. Engine speed was measured using an optical tachometer, and temperature and fuel-consumption measurements were incorporated into the instrumentation system. The test bed was evaluated using a Toyota 7A-FE, 1.8 L, four-cylinder petrol engine under full-load conditions between 1,000 and 5,500 rpm and at different throttle openings at 3,000 rpm. The results showed a maximum recorded torque of 135.5 N·m at 3,000 rpm and a maximum calculated brake power of approximately 56.0 kW at 5,000 rpm. During part-load testing, torque and brake power increased with increasing throttle opening. The reported direct material cost was ₦286,500, excluding labour and overheads. The findings demonstrate the feasibility of locally fabricating an engine test bed for steady-state performance evaluation and engineering education. Further validation is required to verify fuel-consumption and efficiency calculations and to establish the test bed's full design capacity experimentally. Keywords: Automotive engine, engine test bed, hydraulic water-brake dynamometer, brake power, torque measurement, local fabrication
evidence_items.title: Design, Fabrication, and Performance Evaluation of a Locally Developed Automotive Engine Test Bed Using a Hydraulic Water-Brake Dynamometer

evidence_items.summary: Teacher education institutions operate in an increasingly complex higher education environment that requires effective coordination of academic planning, curriculum development, teaching practices, quality assurance, and institutional decision-making. However, the management of these processes may become fragmented when strategic objectives, pedagogical activities, digital resources, and performance evaluation mechanisms are addressed separately. This study aims to develop a conceptual model for the integrated management of educational processes in teacher education institutions. The research is based on a review and conceptual analysis of scholarly literature on educational management, systems theory, quality assurance, institutional leadership, and evidence-informed decision-making in higher education. Comparative analysis and conceptual modelling are employed to identify the principal management functions, their interrelationships, and the mechanisms required to coordinate them within a unified framework. The proposed model comprises six interrelated components: strategic planning, organizational coordination, pedagogical process management, digital information support, monitoring and quality assurance, and feedback-driven improvement. These components are organized within a continuous management cycle encompassing needs analysis, goal setting, planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and corrective action. The model conceptualizes educational process management as a dynamic and interconnected system rather than a collection of isolated administrative activities. Its potential contribution lies in providing a structured framework for aligning institutional priorities, teaching and learning processes, quality indicators, and stakeholder feedback. The study may offer a theoretical and methodological basis for further research and for the development of context-sensitive management practices in teacher education institutions.
evidence_items.title: DEVELOPING AN INTEGRATED MODEL OF EDUCATIONAL PROCESS MANAGEMENT IN TEACHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS

evidence_items.summary: Myocardial calcification is a rare pathological finding that, when extensive myocardial involvement is present, may lead to the development of restrictive cardiomyopathy and progressive heart failure. We report the case of a 57-year-old woman with long-standing heart failure and a restrictive cardiomyopathy phenotype of unknown etiology. Imaging studies demonstrated massive calcium deposits within the left ventricular myocardium and the interventricular septum. Computed tomography initially suggested constrictive pericarditis; however, subsequent echocardiographic assessment and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging supported the diagnosis of restrictive cardiomyopathy secondary to advanced myocardial fibrocalcinosis. No abnormalities of calcium-phosphate metabolism, chronic kidney disease, coronary artery disease, or any other convincing cause of dystrophic or metastatic calcification were identified. Following an extensive differential diagnostic evaluation, a diagnosis of idiopathic massive myocardial calcification was established. This case illustrates the considerable diagnostic challenges in differentiating restrictive cardiomyopathy from constrictive pericarditis and highlights the pivotal role of a multimodality imaging approach in achieving the correct diagnosis.
evidence_items.title: Massive idiopathic myocardial calcification presenting with a restrictive cardiomyopathy phenotype: diagnostic challenges in the differential diagnosis of constrictive pericarditis

evidence_items.summary: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has emerged as a powerful tool for detecting marine biodiversity, particularly for monitoring elusive or endangered species. However, traditional eDNA sampling protocols often rely on small water volumes (≤2 L), which can limit detection sensitivity, especially in vast and dynamic marine environments. Here, we evaluated the effectiveness of large-volume eDNA enrichment (5–50 L) for improving the detection probability of endangered marine species, using metabarcoding and quantitative PCR (qPCR) designed for Balaenoptera brydei (Bryde's Whale). Results showed that the capsule sampler, equipped with a highly folded filter membrane, can filter over 50 L of seawater, significantly increasing eDNA yield and species detection rates compared to standard small-volume sampling (1 L). For metabarcoding results, the large-volume sampling also yielded more total eDNA sequence reads from marine vertebrates and from the endangered Beibu Gulf population of Bryde's Whale, enabling more robust detection of endangered species. Furthermore, combining metabarcoding and qPCR provided complementary detection capabilities for monitoring endangered marine mammals, with metabarcoding enabling broad-spectrum screening and qPCR providing target-specific quantification. Additionally, eDNA samples containing fecal matter were analyzed to explore candidate prey species identification. This result, the detection of eight fish species as candidate prey-associated taxa via large-volume filtration, shows that eDNA enrichment offers a practical, scalable approach. It effectively enhances the sensitivity of marine biodiversity monitoring and provides a valuable tool for conservation programs focused on endangered marine fauna.
evidence_items.title: Large-volume sampling enhances eDNA monitoring of endangered marine species

evidence_items.summary: Fraudulent banking operations bring several problems related to financial safety, reliability of operations, and risk management. The goal of this research is to detect fraudulent operations in banks applying artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques. The methodology includes data preprocessing of banking transactions, missing values' imputation, encoding of categorical features, normalization of numerical features, and random under sampling due to class imbalance problem. Transaction features such as transaction amount, account balance, transaction type, geographical location, transaction frequency, and history of fraud detection are used to discover possible frauds. Machine learning classifiers are used to differentiate between normal operations and fraudulent transactions. The innovation consists in combining transaction-related behavioral characteristics, class imbalance handling, and classifier comparison in fraud recognition framework. There are 50,000 samples in the dataset; among them, there are 47,573 normal transactions, 2,423 fraud transactions, and four samples having no fraud label. According to the given confusion matrix, the framework demonstrates 98.33% accuracy, 98.66% precision, 98.00% recall, and 98.33% F1-score. It proves good classification results for fraud recognition tasks. To get actual values of ROC and AUC, predictions must be calculated for various classification thresholds.

evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly shaping teaching, learning, and research by offering tools that can support educational practice and academic work. This paper examines AI applications in education, their potential benefits, associated challenges, and ethical implications. It considers how AI can assist teachers with lesson planning, instructional materials, assessment, and feedback; support students through personalized learning and explanations of academic concepts; and help researchers with literature searches, data analysis, reference organization, and academic writing. Drawing on a review of existing literature, the paper identifies opportunities to improve educational efficiency, accessibility, and academic productivity. It also highlights concerns involving data privacy, algorithmic bias, inaccurate outputs, academic dishonesty, unequal access to technology, and overdependence on AI tools. The literature points to the importance of user training, ethical guidelines, institutional support, and critical evaluation of AI-generated content (Maphalala & Ajani, 2025; Khatri & Karki, 2023). The paper argues that AI should complement—not replace—teachers, learners, and researchers. Responsible integration requires a balance between technological innovation and human judgment, creativity, critical thinking, and academic integrity.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Teaching, Learning, and Research
